evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 values (all bit patterns including signed zeros, subnormals, and max magnitudes): kernel output vs FP64 asinh gives max abs error 5.68e-7 <= 1e-6 tolerance, 0 violations. The exhaustive domain test leaves no untested legal input, so no violating input exists.

rationale: A degree-9 odd polynomial with 9-digit decimal coefficients plus an FP32 log/sqrt outer branch may not hold a 1e-6 absolute tolerance for all |x| up to 65504, especially near the branch point x=1 and for large magnitudes where FP32 log rounding becomes ~1e-6 absolute.

scope_evidence.summary: Every finite FP16 value is legal ... Every output element must satisfy: abs(actual[i] - asinh(x[i])) <= 1e-6. The relative tolerance is zero. Approximations are permitted if they satisfy this fixed absolute tolerance throughout the entire legal domain.

scope_rationale: Contract requires abs error <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 input across the full legal domain; any violation is a defect.
statement: There exists at least one finite FP16 input x for which the kernel's FP32 output deviates from asinh(x) by more than 1e-6 absolute.
